key_big: Brackets first, then × and ÷, then + and −
body_html:
How it works

An expression such as 30 − 4 × 5 has terms separated by + and −: here 30 and 4 × 5. Work out each term first, then add or subtract: 30 − 20 = 10.

Brackets are worked out first. A minus sign before brackets changes the signs inside: 50 − (12 − 7) = 50 − 12 + 7.

You can often compare expressions without calculating: 78 + 25 = 80 + 23.

Example

Work out 18 + 6 × 4 − 10.

Terms: 18, 6 × 4 = 24, 10

18 + 24 − 10

Answer: 32

Example

Work out 100 − (45 − 15).

100 − 45 + 15

Answer: 70

Common mistakes

  • Working from left to right: 18 + 6 × 4 = 24 × 4 is wrong.
  • Changing only the first sign: 100 − (45 − 15) = 100 − 45 − 15 is wrong.
  • Ignoring the brackets.

faq.q: What is a term in an expression?
faq.a: A part of the expression separated from the others by + or − signs, such as 4 × 5 in 30 − 4 × 5.

faq.q: What is the order of operations?
faq.a: Brackets first, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction.

faq.q: What happens to the signs when a minus is in front of brackets?
faq.a: They change: a − (b + c) = a − b − c and a − (b − c) = a − b + c.
